survivors.label: required_gap
survivors.reason: The public constrained DTW path helper must backtrack an optimal path from an accumulated cost matrix, not just reproduce the supplied three-column fixture. The mutant replaces the predecessor column m-1 by constant 1. At m=3 this can choose a value that belongs to none of the predecessor locations tested in the following if/elif, sending the path to the wrong fallback. For the explicitly supplied nonnegative 4x4 cost matrix in counterexample, the reference-generated D has first candidates [2,11,4], whereas the mutant computes [2,1,4]. It falls to (2,1), subsequently walks through unreachable (1,0), and returns a path containing a forbidden (1,0) step with node-cost 6 rather than the valid diagonal optimum of cost 3. Every selected constrained correctness/purity fixture has at most three columns (or is single-cell), so the changed expression equals m-1 at the first checked backtracking step; the accepted current grade misses this general valid-shape defect. This is source-derived path/arithmetic reasoning, not task code execution or a fresh scored control.
